title: The Effect of Sustainable and Natural Looking on Perceived Aesthetics and Eco-Friendliness in Building Material Evaluation
research_question: This paper aims to investigate the user's perception of materials (sustainable-unsustainable) to evaluate their perception of naturalness, environmental friendliness, and aesthetics through the visual senses.

participants.description: Average age 25.64 years (SD = 8.698). Participants included individuals with eco-related majors (58) and non-eco-related majors (11), representing different educational backgrounds. Gender distribution: 64 male, 48 female. Educational levels ranged from high school to doctor.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Eight picture samples of common building materials, visually presented. These materials were classified into four categories based on two dimensions (naturalness/sustainability): naturalness while sustainable (Hempcrete, Plant-based Polyurethane Rigid Foam, Mycelium, Wool), non-naturalness while sustainable (Bamboo-Wood Fiberboard, Reclaimed Wood), naturalness while unsustainable (Red brick), and non-naturalness while unsustainable (Cement Block).

measures.instrument: Five-point Likert scale (items derived from Overlivet and Soto-Faraco [31])

mechanisms: The surface of the material can affect the judgment of material properties, with closer proximity to the original state making it easier to judge as environmentally friendly and natural.
Morphological integrity influences the extent to which visual features affect judgments of environmental attributes.
Natural perception of interior decoration impacts people's living quality, health, environmental friendliness, and happiness.
People tend to consider solid wood, stone, and brick as more natural and environmentally friendly than synthesized materials.
Processed wood-based composites are perceived as less eco-friendly than less processed materials.
The perception of material naturalness is influenced by the inherent properties of the material ingredients.
implementation_implications: Maintain the naturalness of surface texture during material surface treatment to enhance user demand for natural aesthetic feeling.
Develop more desirable and environmentally friendly alternatives to rare or expensive natural materials (e.g., animal fur, tropical wood) to preserve preference for naturalness and aesthetics.
Utilize findings to help people make healthy and environmentally friendly choices in building materials.

limitations: The study relied solely on visual stimuli (photographs) for material evaluation, not engaging other senses like touch or audition.
Self-report measures (Likert scales) were used for perceived aesthetics, eco-friendliness, and naturalness, which may be subject to social desirability bias.
The study employed a cross-sectional design, limiting the ability to infer causal relationships or observe changes over time.

paper_metadata.title: The Effect of Sustainable and Natural Looking on Perceived Aesthetics and Eco-Friendliness in Building Material Evaluation
paper_metadata.crossref_title: The Effect of Sustainable and Natural Looking on Perceived Aesthetics and Eco-Friendliness in Building Material Evaluation
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: With the development of material synthesis technology, many artificial materials imitating natural materials have emerged in the construction industry. The processing technology of these materials’ surface imitating natural texture is becoming more and more realistic. Some materials are not made of sustainable material but use natural textures to imitate natural materials, attempting to bring users a sense of being close to nature and ecology to attract consumers to use it. However, the intention of use still depends on the user’s other factors like health, aesthetics, and environmental friendliness of the material. Therefore, the challenge for material manufacturers and designers is to understand people’s perceptions of these materials to increase their acceptance by users. This paper aims to investigate the user’s perception of materials (sustainable-unsustainable) to evaluate their perception of naturalness, environmental friendliness, and aesthetics through the visual senses. A total of 112 participants participated in the experiment which was divided into two groups (professional architects and non-professionals). The judgment of non-professionals on the environmental protection of materials imitating natural skin is relatively accurate, which is almost consistent with the judgment of professionals. Results show the importance of maintaining the naturalness of the surface texture in the material, which can enhance the user’s demand for a natural aesthetic feeling. Therefore, it is important to maintain the naturalness of surface texture in the process of material surface treatment. Users’ natural perception of materials will affect their aesthetic perception of materials.
